blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: The first object is a StorageClass: a recipe for making disks. It comes from storage.k8s.io/v1.
blocks.why: Auto Mode creates no StorageClass, as the AWS docs say. You must create one before asking for a disk.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: A recipe for disks, from the storage.k8s.io API

blocks.title: Who makes the disks?
blocks.what: auto-ebs uses Auto Mode’s EBS provisioner. WaitForFirstConsumer waits for a Pod before making a disk.
blocks.why: An EBS volume lives in one zone, so Auto Mode waits to learn which zone the Pod runs in.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the StorageClass, because it needs a provisioner.
blocks.comment: Auto Mode makes an EBS volume once a Pod needs it
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: auto-ebs
provisioner: ebs.csi.eks.amazonaws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer

blocks.title: What kind of disk?
blocks.what: parameters are AWS settings: a gp3 volume, encrypted.
blocks.why: gp3 is the current general-purpose EBS type. Encryption protects the data at rest.
blocks.ifRemoved: Auto Mode uses its defaults: gp3, not encrypted.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: auto-ebs
provisioner: ebs.csi.eks.amazonaws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  type: gp3
  encrypted: "true"

blocks.title: Ask for a disk
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a PersistentVolumeClaim called notes-disk.
blocks.why: A claim asks for storage. The StorageClass decides how to make it.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A second object: a request for a disk
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: auto-ebs
provisioner: ebs.csi.eks.amazonaws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  type: gp3
  encrypted: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: notes-disk

blocks.title: Which recipe?
blocks.what: The claim uses the auto-ebs StorageClass. ReadWriteOnce means one node at a time can use it.
blocks.why: An EBS volume attaches to one machine at a time.
blocks.ifRemoved: The cluster’s default StorageClass is used. Auto Mode has none, so the claim waits forever.
blocks.comment: Use auto-ebs, attached to one node at a time
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: auto-ebs
provisioner: ebs.csi.eks.amazonaws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  type: gp3
  encrypted: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: notes-disk
spec:
  storageClassName: auto-ebs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce

blocks.title: How big?
blocks.why: Pay for what you need. An EBS volume can grow later, but never shrink.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the claim, because it must say how much storage it needs.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: auto-ebs
provisioner: ebs.csi.eks.amazonaws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  type: gp3
  encrypted: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: notes-disk
spec:
  storageClassName: auto-ebs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi

blocks.title: A Pod to use it
blocks.what: Three dashes start a third object: a Pod called notes.
blocks.why: The Pod writes to the disk so you can see the data survive.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A third object: a Pod that writes to the disk
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: auto-ebs
provisioner: ebs.csi.eks.amazonaws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  type: gp3
  encrypted: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: notes-disk
spec:
  storageClassName: auto-ebs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: notes

blocks.title: Write the start time
blocks.what: busybox adds the current time to /data/starts, then sleeps.
blocks.why: Each time the Pod starts, the file gains a line.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Pod, because it has nothing to run.
blocks.comment: Add a line to /data/starts each time the container starts
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: auto-ebs
provisioner: ebs.csi.eks.amazonaws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  type: gp3
  encrypted: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: notes-disk
spec:
  storageClassName: auto-ebs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: notes
spec:
  containers:
    - name: notes
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "date >> /data/starts && sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Where the disk appears
blocks.what: volumeMounts puts the volume named disk at /data inside the container.
blocks.why: Files written under /data go to the EBS volume.
blocks.ifRemoved: Files under /data go to the container’s own storage, lost when the Pod goes.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: auto-ebs
provisioner: ebs.csi.eks.amazonaws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  type: gp3
  encrypted: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: notes-disk
spec:
  storageClassName: auto-ebs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: notes
spec:
  containers:
    - name: notes
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "date >> /data/starts && sleep 3600"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: disk
          mountPath: /data

blocks.title: Which claim?
blocks.what: The volume named disk comes from the notes-disk claim. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: The claim outlives the Pod, so a new Pod finds the same data.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Pod, because the mount names a volume that does not exist.
blocks.comment: The volume is the notes-disk claim
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: auto-ebs
provisioner: ebs.csi.eks.amazonaws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  type: gp3
  encrypted: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: notes-disk
spec:
  storageClassName: auto-ebs
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: notes
spec:
  containers:
    - name: notes
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "date >> /data/starts && sleep 3600"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: disk
          mountPath: /data
  volumes:
    - name: disk
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: notes-disk

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version. StorageClass is in storage.k8s.io/v1; the others are in core v1.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.StorageClass:kind: A recipe for making disks on demand.
notes.PersistentVolumeClaim:kind: A request for storage, which a StorageClass fulfils.
notes.Pod:kind: A Pod runs one or more containers together.
notes.StorageClass:metadata.name: The recipe’s name. Claims choose it with storageClassName.
notes.PersistentVolumeClaim:metadata.name: The claim’s name. The Pod refers to it.
notes.Pod:metadata.name: The Pod’s name.
notes.provisioner: ebs.csi.eks.amazonaws.com: EKS Auto Mode’s built-in EBS support.
notes.volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer: make the volume once a Pod using it is placed, in that Pod’s zone.
notes.parameters: AWS settings for each volume. Values are text.
notes.parameters.type: gp3: the general-purpose SSD volume type.
notes.parameters.encrypted: Encrypt the volume with the default aws/ebs key. Quotes keep it text.
notes.Pod:spec: What the Pod runs, and which volumes it uses.
notes.spec.storageClassName: Which StorageClass makes the disk: auto-ebs.
notes.spec.accessModes: How the volume can be used. Each list item is one mode.
notes.spec.accessModes[]: ReadWriteOnce: one node at a time can read and write.
notes.spec.resources: How much storage the claim needs.
notes.spec.containers: The containers in this Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name.
notes.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.containers[].command: Add the time to /data/starts, then sleep for an hour.
notes.spec.containers[].volumeMounts: Where volumes appear inside the container.
notes.spec.containers[].volumeMounts[].name: Which volume: disk, defined under volumes.
notes.spec.volumes: Volumes the Pod can mount. Each list item is one volume.
notes.spec.volumes[].name: The volume’s name, used by volumeMounts.
notes.spec.volumes[].persistentVolumeClaim: The volume comes from a claim.

tryIt.result: Creates the StorageClass, the claim, and the Pod.
STATUS turns Bound once the Pod is placed. Auto Mode has made a 1Gi EBS volume.
Removes the Pod. It takes up to 30 seconds, because sleep ignores the stop signal.
Creates the Pod again. The claim and its volume were never deleted.
Prints two start times. The new Pod found the old data.
Removes all three. Auto Mode deletes the EBS volume too, because the reclaim policy is Delete.

questions.question: When does Auto Mode create the EBS volume?
answers: When a Pod using the claim is placed on a node
questions.explain: WaitForFirstConsumer waits for a Pod, so the volume is made in that Pod’s zone.

questions.question: The Pod is deleted and created again. What is in /data/starts?
answers: The earlier lines plus a new one
questions.explain: The claim and its volume outlive the Pod, so the data stays.

questions.question: Which provisioner belongs to EKS Auto Mode?
questions.explain: ebs.csi.aws.com is the separately installed EBS CSI driver. Auto Mode has its own.

fix.explain: Many guides assume a StorageClass called gp3. Auto Mode creates none, so the claim stays Pending.
fix.fix: Name the StorageClass this file creates: storageClassName: auto-ebs.
